questions.q: What should you do before crossing the road?
questions.exp: Stopping to look and listen gives you time to judge traffic before you commit to crossing.

questions.q: Why is it dangerous to walk in front of a stopped bus?
opts: The driver can't see you there — it's a blind spot
questions.exp: The area right in front of, behind, or beside a bus is a blind spot — the driver may not know you're there.

questions.q: If you see a broken traffic light nearby, you should:
opts: Report it so it can be fixed
questions.exp: Reporting hazards means they can be fixed before someone gets hurt.

questions.q: On a road with no pavement, you should walk:
opts: In the exact middle of the road
questions.exp: Facing traffic lets you see vehicles coming and react — walking with your back to traffic removes that warning time.

questions.q: Roughly what share of Kenyan road deaths are pedestrians?
questions.exp: Pedestrians make up roughly 4 in 10 road deaths in Kenya — a very high share compared to many countries.

questions.q: As a boda boda passenger, you should:
opts: Sit fully seated, feet on footrests, helmet on
questions.exp: A stable, seated position with a fastened helmet gives you the best protection if the bike stops suddenly.

questions.q: How many extra passengers can legally ride on a boda boda at once?
opts: As many as can hold on
questions.exp: Kenyan law limits a boda boda to one passenger — extra riders make the bike unstable and harder to control.

questions.q: Under current rules, who must wear a helmet on a boda boda?
questions.exp: Helmets are compulsory for both rider and passenger — a head injury can happen to either.

questions.q: What is the minimum age generally recommended before a child rides as a boda boda passenger?
questions.exp: Younger children often can't hold on securely or judge balance, so around 12 is the general guidance — arrange other transport before then.

questions.q: Under the Traffic Act, riding a boda boda on the pavement is:
opts: Not allowed — pavements are for pedestrians
questions.exp: Pavements are reserved for pedestrians — a boda boda riding there puts walkers at risk.

questions.q: What should a safe boda boda rider have?
opts: Registration with a licensed SACCO or company and visible ID
questions.exp: Registered riders are accountable to a SACCO or company and carry visible ID — a useful safety check before boarding.

questions.q: When is it safe to board a bus or matatu?
opts: Only after it has fully stopped
From the middle of the road
questions.exp: A moving vehicle can lurch or brake suddenly — always wait for a complete stop first.

questions.q: A matatu's seating capacity is fixed by its licence. If it's already full, you should:
opts: Wait for the next one or an official one
questions.exp: An overloaded vehicle is harder to control and slower to stop — it's safer to wait for the next one.

questions.q: The safest place to cross near a matatu stage is:
opts: Right in front of the parked matatu
A clear spot with good visibility, away from parked vehicles
questions.exp: Parked vehicles block a driver's view of you and your view of oncoming traffic — cross where you can see and be seen.

questions.q: NTSA rules for school transport vehicles require them to have:
opts: A speed governor and regular inspection
Only a driver, no other checks
questions.exp: A speed governor and regular inspection help keep school transport vehicles within safe operating limits.

questions.q: If a bus, matatu, or boda is overtaking dangerously while you're a passenger, you should:
opts: Say nothing and hope for the best
Ask calmly to be let out at the next safe stop
questions.exp: Asking to alight at the next safe stop removes you from danger without creating a new one.

questions.q: A traffic light turns amber. What does it mean?
opts: Prepare to stop and stay alert
questions.exp: Amber is a warning phase — it means the light is about to change, not a signal to rush.

questions.q: A red traffic light means:
opts: Go if the road looks clear
questions.exp: Red always means a full stop, regardless of how clear the road looks.

questions.q: A round sign with a red border, showing a vehicle, usually means:
opts: That type of vehicle is not allowed here
questions.exp: Red-circle signs are prohibition signs — they tell you something is not allowed.

questions.q: A triangular road sign with an exclamation mark usually means:
questions.exp: Triangular signs warn of a hazard ahead so you can slow down and stay alert.

questions.q: A blue circular sign showing a pedestrian and an arrow means:
questions.exp: Blue circular signs give a mandatory instruction — here, that pedestrians must use the marked path.

questions.q: A sign showing a number inside a red circle, like a speed limit sign, means:
opts: Maximum speed limit — do not exceed it
questions.exp: A number in a red circle sets the maximum legal speed for that stretch of road.

questions.q: Best way to be seen walking at dusk?
opts: Walk in the middle of the road
questions.exp: Bright or reflective clothing catches headlights and gives drivers more time to spot you.

questions.q: When do Kenyan roads see the highest number of crashes, according to national data?
questions.exp: Friday to Sunday evenings are flagged as the deadliest window in Kenya's National Road Safety Action Plan.

questions.q: What's a safer habit at dusk or night as a pedestrian?
opts: Wear dark clothing to look neat
Assume every driver has seen you
questions.exp: Never assume you've been seen — bright or reflective clothing gives drivers a real chance to spot you in time.

questions.q: Walking somewhere unlit at night, the safest habit is to:
opts: Stick to known, busier routes and carry a light
Walk with headphones at full volume
questions.exp: Familiar, busier routes plus a phone torch or small light make you both safer and more visible.

questions.q: Fatigue affects a driver or rider's reaction time:
opts: Almost as much as alcohol can
questions.exp: Tiredness slows reaction time significantly — worth remembering on late trips as a passenger too.

questions.q: Why is an overloaded matatu or lorry more dangerous?
opts: It takes longer to stop and can roll on bends
questions.exp: Extra weight increases stopping distance and makes a vehicle more likely to tip over on a bend.

questions.q: If a vehicle you're about to board already looks full, you should:
opts: Wait for the next one or a licensed one
Offer to hold someone's luggage instead
questions.exp: Waiting for a properly loaded vehicle is safer than adding to an already overloaded one.

questions.q: A driver who seems drowsy on a long trip is a warning sign because:
opts: Tired drivers react much more slowly, similar to being impaired
Drowsiness always shows clearly on their face
questions.exp: Fatigue slows reaction time in a way that's comparable to alcohol impairment, even if it isn't obvious to look at.

questions.q: On a wet road, a vehicle's stopping distance is:
questions.exp: Water reduces tyre grip, so vehicles need much more distance to stop safely in the rain.

questions.q: As a pedestrian in heavy rain, you should:
opts: Give vehicles extra space since they may skid
Walk closer to the road to avoid puddles
Assume drivers can stop as fast as usual
questions.exp: Vehicles are more likely to skid in the rain, so extra distance protects you if one loses grip.

questions.q: Flooded sections of road are risky mainly because they can:
questions.exp: Standing water can hide dangerous gaps in the road surface, so it's safer to avoid wading or driving through it.

questions.q: When should you be most alert for animals crossing rural roads?
opts: Dawn, dusk, or near grazing land
questions.exp: Livestock and wildlife move more near dawn, dusk, or grazing areas, so extra caution helps at those times.

questions.q: If you see a herd of animals near or on the road, you should:
opts: Slow down and give them a wide, patient berth
questions.exp: Animals can be unpredictable, so slowing down and leaving space is safer than rushing or assuming they'll clear the road.

questions.q: Why is looking at your phone while crossing the road risky?
opts: It isn't risky if the sound is on
It slows your reaction time and narrows your attention
Phones don't affect walking at all
It only matters for drivers, not pedestrians
questions.exp: Even with sound on, a phone screen pulls your visual attention away from traffic and slows how fast you notice danger.

questions.q: The safest habit with your phone near traffic is to:
opts: Put it away before stepping off the curb
Use it only in one hand
questions.exp: Putting the phone away before you cross removes the distraction completely, rather than trying to manage it.
